newsitem.title: MEXICO: Argentina sugar consumption seen little changed.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sugar consumption seen little changed.

text.p: Argentina's sugar consumption has changed little in the last three crop years and is seen not moving much in this 1996-1997 cycle, the senior analyst of tropical commodities for Sparks Companies Inc said here Thursday.
Peter Buzzanell told the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference that in the 1990s there was a resurgence of sugar use in Argentina, moving to a record 1.31 million tonnes in 1994-1995.
"Consumption the last two years has been relatively unchanged as Argentina has gone through a recession," he said.
Argentina's sugar use grew to 1.04 million tonnes in 1984-1985 from 983,000 tonnes in the mid-1970s, but then slipped under one million tonnes in the late 1980s, he added.
Buzzanell said Argentina has a small but established corn sweetner sector, which at one stage had four plants in the country producing around 200,000 tonnes of product annually.

"Argentina's corn sweetner manufacturers and the resulting HFCS (high fructose corn syrup) consumption has suffered the last two years due to the weak economy coupled with relatively low domestic sugar prices and extremely high corn prices," Buzzanell said.
He added the difficult operating conditions in 1995 and early 1996 forced changes in the HFCS sector.

"CPC closed its Cordoba factory and concentrated its operations in its remaining plant. The net loss of capacity will be largely offset by the expansion being undertaken by Argentina's largest HFCS producer, Industrias de Maiz (IMASA), with the planned first stage of growth in HFCS-55 capacity at IMASA's Chacabuco plant," Buzzanell said.

CPC International Inc is a corn syrup producer in the U.S. It has a joint venture in Mexico -- Arancia Corn Products, with a 18,000 tonne-per-month plant in Queretaro state, with plans to boost that to 60,000 tonnes per month.
